text: 🔥🇲🇽 "In the end, the final beneficiary was the same Casillas brothers in every case." — Raquel Buenrostro, Secretary of Anti-Corruption and Good Government, Mañanera, Nov 5, 2026 Using open sources, Buenrostro traced the network to 1983, when the Hernández Casillas brothers entered the Interior Ministry, and later CISEN. By 1999 they were electoral suppliers in the State of Mexico, where a 2005 contract scandal forced seven electoral councilors to resign. From 2014 to 2023, 23 of the 32 state electoral bodies gave their companies more than 2 billion pesos in contracts; in 2024-25, 15 bodies gave 646 million. The firms rigged bids among themselves, declared no employees, shared addresses and phones, and moved money through layers of companies, down to 96-year-olds and 18-year-olds. The Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF) has frozen the assets of 25 people and 15 companies.

🔥🇲🇽 "That's where this whole mess, this electoral mafia, comes from. It did not arise with Taddei." "Who appointed those electoral councilors? You, and all the INE councilors from 2014 to 2023." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 5, 2026 Sheinbaum traced the companies behind the electoral-materials contracts to the Hernández Casillas brothers, who started out in the 1980s under Juan Carlos Padilla Aguilar at Renapo and then CISEN. Padilla, she said, is today a prominent member of Somos, which she called Lorenzo Córdova's party. From 2014 to 2023, the INE council led by Córdova appointed every state electoral council, and those bodies gave the brothers' companies more than 2 billion pesos in contracts. Former INE head Guadalupe Taddei must be investigated, she said, "but it was not born there."

🚨🇲🇽 "Raids against people because of their skin color and their ethnic origin." "It's sort of logical to think that something that influenced Latinos who have the right to vote in the United States to now vote for the Democratic Party would have to do with this racism." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 5, 2026 Asked whether the Trump administration's immigration raids shaped Tuesday's US midterm results, Sheinbaum said "it's very likely." Post-election analyses show that many Latino voters, among them US citizens of Mexican origin who backed Trump in 2024, voted Democratic this time. A day earlier she had highlighted the wins of the Mexican-origin governors-elect of California and Texas.

🇲🇽⚖️ "With everything we know now, savings can very probably be made within the INE." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 5, 2026 Under Guadalupe Taddei, the INE requested close to 47 billion pesos for 2027. The government disagreed, but by law it must send autonomous bodies' budget requests to Congress exactly as presented. It removed only the part tied to a possible 2027 public consultation, which will not take place. Sheinbaum said it is up to the Chamber of Deputies to cut the INE's budget and bring it in line with 2024, 2025 and 2026. A reporter noted Taddei had also sought an atypical increase of more than 2 billion pesos for the INE's administration directorate, 75% above 2024.

🇲🇽🎨 "The lies crash into the truth and into reality." — "Lie Detector" segment, Mañanera, Nov 5, 2026 In 2026 the well-being scholarships reach more than 19.5 million public school students. El Universal's front page attributed to UNESCO a figure suggesting the Benito Juárez scholarships discourage students. The Education Ministry (SEP) clarified it is not a UNESCO position but an academic working paper, with an estimate about a different population than the one the scholarships serve. One of its authors, Fernanda Márquez Padilla Casar, studied at a private institution from 2004 to 2010 on a Pemex scholarship. She is the daughter of María Amparo Casar, president of Mexicanos contra la Corrupción.

🇲🇽🌎 "There will be a bilateral meeting with the government of China, with the President of China." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 5, 2026 Sheinbaum confirmed her trip to the APEC summit in China. She leaves early Sunday, Nov 15, and is back by Nov 20; the Interior Secretary will host the mañaneras that week. Several bilateral meetings are being arranged, including one with President Xi Jinping and Chinese ministers. It is not yet confirmed that Trump will attend: "If he goes, of course, we're interested in meeting with him." A day earlier, she said Mexico has a very good relationship with both China and the United States.

text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "A good part of the Hernández Casillas companies are coyotes. They don't even produce. They are intermediary companies." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 5, 2026 Sheinbaum announced a decree next week to strengthen Talleres Gráficos de México, the state printer that makes the federal ballots, "so that most electoral materials are made in the Mexican state's company." Its board, now just the Interior, Anti-Corruption and Finance ministries, will add more ministries, the Superior Audit Office as an observer, and academics from UNAM, IPN or Tec de Monterrey. For ballot boxes and voting screens, she called for open bidding with clear guidelines and unit prices, so that one state doesn't pay ten times what another pays for the same thing. The Superior Audit Office will audit every state electoral body.

🇲🇽📉 <u>Banxico Surprises: Rate Cut to 6.25%</u>

Banco de México cut its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 6.25% on Thursday, by majority vote, after holding at 6.50% since May. The market expected no change. El Financiero notes that Banxico had already said it would not "copy" the Fed. The rate gap with the US was at a record low of 250 basis points.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum Moves Ballot Printing Back to the State</u>

After exposing a network of family firms that held INE and state electoral contracts for 27 years, worth more than 2.6 billion pesos, Sheinbaum announced a decree requiring Talleres Gráficos de México, the state printer, to produce most official election materials. The ASF will act as an observer, with academics taking part. Ballot boxes and voting booths will go to Mexican firms through bids with clear prices and a chain of custody. "This didn't start with Taddei," she said.
